title: User lifecycle - create a user inside a discovered LOB, then prove it exists
why: The owner's example, built as a real chain: LOB -> user group -> create user -> fetch it back -> check the transaction was recorded. The created user's id is carried from the create response into the verification, so nothing is hardcoded and nothing is assumed.

hops.name: SetUserDetails
hops.note: expect_created makes the assertion reject Success:true + Message:'Already Exists' - a no-op that a status check would score as a pass. The username is unique per run, so this inserts rather than colliding.

hops.name: GetAllActiveUserList
hops.note: Matched on UserId, not on name: the product upper-cases UserName, so a case-sensitive name assert fails against a correctly created user. ~1.1 MB response, no filter parameter exists - the search is client-side.

hops.name: GetLogDetails
hops.note: The transaction-recorded hop. Wired and reachable, but this reader needs filter parameters beyond LogTypeId that are not yet known, so it currently returns 'No Records Found'. Reported as-is rather than guessed.
